main_body: Tall brick shopfront building with a slate mansard roof, two dormers, a chimney, a balcony and a striped awning over a shop window
top_band: No distinct top surface. Rows ~10-18 are a flat grey-teal band that reads as a parapet or rooftop face, and rows ~20-42 are slate drawn as a near-vertical face with dormers. The only thin horizontal feature is the orange cornice at rows ~43-45.
evidence: The facade is drawn straight on, like an architectural elevation. Windows, the balcony, the awning and the shop front are all flat vertical faces. The roof is a vertical slate wall with dormers, not a foreshortened slope seen from above. No horizontal roof surface reads as a top band: the teal strip is the top of the parapet seen face-on, and the cornice is only 2-3 rows. Unlike the references, whose roofs are large sloped surfaces, this building has no readable top surface.

style.evidence: The brick has several tones with per-brick variation. The slate has multiple blue-grey steps with joints. The warm window glow has speckle highlights, and the awning, cornice and stone trim are each shaded in steps. Outlines lean dark brown or dark blue-grey beside each material rather than being neutral black. The roof deck and the shopfront base are somewhat flatter, but overall the piece is as rich as the Beodeul house references.
